maint.restore_warn: Current devices, profiles, accounts and settings will be REPLACED by those in the backup. Kut restarts, all sessions are closed and the sign-in password reverts to the backup's. Right before restoring, an automatic backup of the current state is taken, so you can go back to it too.
maint.owner_why: A backup carries every account's password hash, the 2FA secrets and the server's private key; so a session is not enough and the owner password is required.
maint.owner_pw: Owner password (current password of the admin account)
maint.moved_note: This backup comes from another server. The private key stays the same and the old devices' configs keep working; only the address they connect to matters.
maint.port_note: The WireGuard port in the backup is {port} (currently {current} on this server). After restoring, UDP {port} must be open in the cloud firewall and in ufw.
maint.subnet_note: The VPN subnet will become {subnet} instead of {current}.
maint.change_endpoint_hint: Device configs connect to this address. Check it if the new server's IP or domain name differs; existing devices' configs must then carry the same address (if you use a domain name, pointing its DNS at the new server is enough).
maint.owner_hint: Creating, downloading, restoring and deleting backups and these settings are available only to the owner account (admin).
maint.pass_set_ph: Passphrase is set; type a new one to change it
maint.pass_none_ph: Leave empty and backups are unencrypted
maint.enc_off: Encryption is off (backups are plain files).
maint.sizes: Backups: {backups} · log archive: {archive} · traffic history: {history} · folder: {dir}
maint.download_why: The backup from {when} will be downloaded to your computer.
maint.pass_change_why: The backup encryption passphrase will change.
maint.enc_off_why: Backup encryption will be turned off.
maint.backup_now_why: A manual backup will be taken.
maint.backup_intro: A backup contains the devices, profiles, accounts, settings and the activity log. Since the server's private key is inside, I recommend encrypting it with a passphrase. Backups live on the server's own disk: if the disk fails they go with it, so download one to your computer now and then. To move to another server, install Kut there, then supply the backup with “Restore from file…”.
maint.pass_hint: Encrypted with AES-256. The passphrase is kept on this server in a file only root can read so that automatic backups can be encrypted; the aim is to protect a backup you download or copy elsewhere from leaking. Write the passphrase down separately: it is asked when restoring on a new server, and if you lose it the encrypted backups cannot be opened. When the passphrase changes only new backups use the new one.
maint.auto_backup_hint: Kut takes a backup by itself when it is due. If the server is off at that time, it takes it once it starts.
maint.enc_off_confirm: Later backups will be unencrypted. Old encrypted backups can still be opened with the passphrase, but the passphrase is deleted from this server; make sure you have written it down.
maint.retention_intro: So the log does not grow without bound, old events are removed from it after the set period. If the option below is on, they are first written to monthly compressed files (logs/activity-YYYY-MM.jsonl.gz) and deleted when the archive period ends. Traffic charts are kept for up to 30 days and survive service restarts.
maint.log_days: How long to keep the log
maint.archive_hint: When off, expired events are simply deleted.
maint.owner_only: Only the owner account (admin) can change these settings.
maint.service_intro: Restarts Kut. WireGuard connections are not interrupted; the panel is unresponsive for a few seconds and the page refreshes by itself when it is back. This already happens automatically on restore and version upgrade; use it only when something is stuck.
maint.restart_confirm: The panel goes down for a few seconds, then the page refreshes. VPN connections are not affected.
